### What the Dishonest Manager Did Right
Author: Rick Warren
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/daily-hope-with-rick-warren/daily-hope-with-rick-warren-january-25-2020.html
Passage: Luke 16:4
Points:
- Jesus does not endorse the manager's deceit, but commends his practical foresight and decisiveness.
- Sound financial stewardship requires looking beyond immediate desires toward the eternal future.
- Faithful management begins with establishing an intentional financial plan and budget.
- Believers must act promptly rather than procrastinating on necessary adjustments.
- Investing worldly resources in ways that please God yields everlasting dividends.

### Passing the Stewardship Test?
Author: Will Graham
Site: Billy Graham Evangelistic Association
URL: https://billygraham.org/articles/will-graham-devotion-the-unfaithful-servant
Passage: Luke 16:10
Points:
- Unfaithfulness in our responsibilities damages our Christian witness and discredits our testimony.
- Disorganization and neglect in daily duties can destroy trust and harm personal reputation.
- Continued wastefulness risks the loss of the stewardship opportunities God has provided.
- Faithfulness in small, routine matters demonstrates readiness for larger spiritual responsibilities.

### Jesus Commends Shrewd Money Managers
Author: Jon Bloom
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/jesus-commends-shrewd-money-managers
Passage: Luke 16:8-9
Points:
- Worldly people frequently exercise more initiative for earthly survival than believers do for the kingdom.
- The manager wisely recognized his impending loss and used his master's resources to secure a future home.
- Kingdom shrewdness calls believers to use temporary earthly resources generously to bless others.
- How we steward money serves as an earthly proving ground for true, eternal riches.
